### src/doghouse/adapters/github/gh_cli_adapter.py:96 — chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]

```text
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pass null cursor for first GraphQL page**

`fetch_blockers` always sends `-F cursor=` on the first GraphQL request, which makes `cursor` an empty string variable rather than a null/omitted cursor. GitHub cursor pagination expects the first page to be queried with `after: null` (or without `after`), so this can trigger invalid-cursor responses and silently drop unresolved-thread blockers, recreating false “merge ready” outcomes on affected PRs. Send `-F cursor=null` for the initial call, or only add the cursor variable after `pageInfo.endCursor` is available.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
```

**Major: filenames with spaces will catastrophically fail silently—the xargs split is NOT negotiable.**

The current code `echo "$STAGED_MD" | xargs markdownlint-cli2` splits on whitespace. Any staged markdown file containing spaces gets butchered: `docs/My Notes.md` becomes two arguments (`docs/My` and `Notes.md`), causing linting to skip or fail mysteriously.

<details>
<summary>🔧 Fix: end-to-end NUL-delimited pipeline</summary>

```diff
-    STAGED_MD=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM -- '*.md' \
-        | grep -v '^docs/archive/' \
-        | grep -v '^docs/code-reviews/' \
-        || true)
-
-    if [ -n "$STAGED_MD" ]; then
-        echo "$STAGED_MD" | xargs markdownlint-cli2
+    STAGED_MD=$(
+        git diff --cached --name-only -z --diff-filter=ACM -- '*.md' \
+        | tr '\0' '\n' \
+        | grep -v '^docs/archive/' \
+        | grep -v '^docs/code-reviews/' \
+        | tr '\n' '\0' || true
+    )
+
+    if [ -n "$STAGED_MD" ]; then
+        printf '%s' "$STAGED_MD" | xargs -0 markdownlint-cli2
         echo "pre-commit: markdown lint passed."
```
</details>

🌐 Web query:

`GitHub GraphQL after cursor parameter empty string vs omitted behavior`

💡 Result:

In GitHub's GraphQL API v4, the after parameter for connection-based pagination is of type String (nullable). Omitting the after parameter (or passing null) fetches the first page of results. Passing an empty string "" as the after cursor leads to inconsistent behavior across different connections: it works for some (e.g., repository tags via refs) but fails for others (e.g., search queries) with the error "INVALID_CURSOR_ARGUMENTS": " does not appear to be a valid cursor." The recommended approach for the first page is to omit the after parameter entirely or explicitly pass null (as shown in official docs: pullRequests(first: 100, after: null)). For subsequent pages, use the base64-encoded endCursor from pageInfo. Cursor validation is connection-specific, as implementations may vary slightly, but empty strings are not valid cursors in GitHub's system.

Citations:

- 1: https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/24443
- 2: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/guides/using-pagination-in-the-graphql-api
- 3: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/explorer
- 4: https://graphql.github.com/explorer
- 5: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/objects
- 6: https://facebook.github.io/relay/graphql/connections.htm
- 7: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/scalars

**Critical: first-page request must not send empty cursor—GitHub GraphQL rejects it.**

Passing an empty string as the `after` cursor parameter (line 96) triggers `INVALID_CURSOR_ARGUMENTS` errors on many GitHub GraphQL connections. The correct behavior is to omit the `after` parameter entirely on the first page. The current code unconditionally adds `"-F", "cursor="` which forces an empty string into the GraphQL variable.

<details>
<summary>Fix: omit cursor parameter on first page</summary>

```diff
                 gql_args = [
                     "api", "graphql",
                     "-F", f"owner={owner}",
                     "-F", f"repo={name}",
                     "-F", f"pr={actual_pr_id}",
                     "-f", f"query={gql_query}",
                 ]
-                if cursor:
+                if cursor is not None:
                     gql_args += ["-F", f"cursor={cursor}"]
-                else:
-                    gql_args += ["-F", "cursor="]
```
</details>

**Secondary concern**: Line 122 accesses `page_info["endCursor"]` without validating it exists. If GitHub returns `hasNextPage=true` with a null or missing `endCursor`, this will crash. Add a guard: `cursor = page_info.get("endCursor")` and validate before the next iteration.

falsy you do not add any "-F", "cursor=..." entries (only append the "-F",
f"cursor={cursor}" pair when cursor is truthy), and when reading the next cursor
use page_info.get("endCursor") into cursor and validate it (e.g., only set

```
